ai.description: *Hemidactylus garnotii* (Gekkonidae) reaches 12 cm. It is greyish-brown with a pale, yellow-orange underside and a flattened, unsegmented tail. Distinguishing features include smooth scales and toe pads.
ai.identificationRemarks: Distinguish the Fox Gecko (*Hemidactylus garnotii*) by its distinctively flattened, leaf-like tail with serrated edges, which lacks the prominent tubercles found on other species.
ai.habitat: The Fox Gecko inhabits tropical moist forests and human-altered landscapes, typically ranging from sea level up to 1,500 meters in elevation across the Indian subcontinent.
ai.behavior: The Fox Gecko is primarily nocturnal and utilizes a "sit-and-wait" foraging strategy, remaining motionless to ambush insects attracted to artificial lights.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Hemidactylus garnotii* is an obligate parthenogen that reproduces without males. They lay clutches of two hard-shelled eggs, typically breeding throughout the year.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Hemidactylus garnotii* occurs across Northeast India, the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, and parts of the Western Ghats, ranging from sea level to mid-elevations.
